therapeutic_hypothesis.proposed_mechanism: bispecific antibody-mediated receptor blockade and antibody-dependent cytotoxicity
therapeutic_hypothesis.intended_biology: inhibition of EGFR/MET-driven tumor proliferation and survival combined with immune-mediated tumor cell killing
therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: Adults with advanced or metastatic NSCLC harboring EGFR exon 20 insertion mutations
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: Progression-Free Survival (PFS) by BICR per RECIST v1.1

results.effect_size: Median PFS 11.37 months (amivantamab + chemo) vs 6.70 months (chemo alone); HR 0.395 (95% CI 0.296–0.528)
safety_signals: Serious adverse events including pneumonia, rash pustular, skin infection, and cellulitis were more frequent in the amivantamab + chemotherapy arm
Infusion-related reactions are a known class effect of amivantamab

dose_info.dose: Amivantamab 1400 mg (1750 mg if ≥80 kg) escalating to 1750 mg (2100 mg if ≥80 kg) from Cycle 3; Pemetrexed 500 mg/m²; Carboplatin AUC 5
dose_info.schedule: Amivantamab weekly up to Cycle 2 Day 1, then Day 1 of each 21-day cycle; Pemetrexed Day 1 of each 21-day cycle then maintenance; Carboplatin Day 1 of each 21-day cycle for up to 4 cycles

context.indication: Advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer with EGFR exon 20 insertions
context.duration: Up to 29 months for primary endpoint; up to 5 years 3 months for secondary endpoints

modulation_entries.hypothesis: Amivantamab-mediated EGFR/MET blockade and ADCC may sensitize tumor cells to DNA damage and enhance apoptotic response to platinum-based chemotherapy, improving overall anti-tumor efficacy
modulation_entries.citation: HR 0.395 (95% CI: 0.296–0.528), p = <0.0001 for PFS of amivantamab + chemotherapy vs chemotherapy alone

modulation_entries.hypothesis: Amivantamab-mediated EGFR/MET blockade may enhance anti-proliferative effects of pemetrexed by suppressing survival signaling that could otherwise compensate for nucleotide synthesis inhibition
